summary: Follow-up to last week's degradation event. Focus was on validating rollback and fallback procedures, verifying KMS rotation interactions with cached KV sessions, and rebuilding customer trust via an observable dry-run. Agreed to run a non-disruptive rollback in staging with full telemetry capture and a post-dry-run retro. Discussed longtail eviction patterns and prioritized mitigations (prefix cache tuning, autoscaler thresholds, alert thresholds).
topics: KMS / key rotation impact on KV cache
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-07-19 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood CSM), Maya (BlueLoom SRE), Ethan (BlueLoom ML Ops), Priya (BlueLoom Security), Jordan (BlueLoom Product)

Summary (auto): quick follow-up to the July 12th partial degradation where a subset of long-running chat sessions experienced high tail latency and some KV cache evictions. This call is to rehearse rollbacks and confirm a plan to capture evidence and reduce blast radius.

---
00:00 Jamie: hey everyone thanks for making time today um i know we promised a short dry-run planning session so i'll kick us off. can folks hear me okay?
00:07 Maya: yeah loud and clear, thanks.
00:11 Samir: hi, quick note, i pulled the last flamegraph export and the hot path was in kv eviction + attention cache re-warm, not the tokenization.
00:22 Ethan: that matches what we saw — but just to be clear, the evictions coincided with our nightly KMS rotation attempt? or is that conflating events?
00:34 Priya: so the rotation did start at 02:14 UTC but we had a staggered schedule, i can confirm whether any job held an active session key.
00:43 Jamie: ok good. hypothesis A was autoscaler spike + a concurrent KMS rotation -> some requests missed the cached KV and forced full state rehydrate which pushed latency. hypothesis B was memory fragmentation on the model worker that made the eviction algorithm more aggressive.
01:03 Jordan: and from product perspective customers saw a 5–10s tail on chat completions and a handful of errors flagged as 502 upstream, right?
01:12 Lina: yep, customer ticket numbers in the shared deck, cc: support thread.
01:18 Maya: quick correction — it was more like intermittent 3–12s tails, a couple of 502s when replays hit the legacy endpoint. transcription note: the timeline in the spreadsheet has the wrong timezone stamped (pdt vs utc) so i adjusted.
01:35 Samir: great catch. for the dry-run we suggested a non-disruptive rollback flow: 1) lock new deployments, 2) scale down to a prior model runtime snapshot (we call old-run), 3) route 10% smoke traffic for 15 min, 4) observe kv hit/miss metrics and token latency.
01:59 Ethan: are we comfortable automating the route-back? i ask because earlier the fallback logic did some unexpected model variant routing which increased token size and i want to avoid cascading differences.
02:12 Jamie: we won't automate in prod for this dry-run — we'll do explicit manual route changes in staging with an ops runbook step. Samir will walk through the exact commands.
02:23 Samir: sure. command sequence is in the runbook, but note transcribed commands sometimes lose dashes. it's: redwood rollback --target snapshot-2028-07-07 --route staging/smoke --observe 900s. i'll post the exact snippet to the drive.
02:44 Priya: quick security question — if we route to an older snapshot, do we need a different KMS key or will the existing credential chain handle it? our concern is key rotation invalidating in-memory sessions.
02:58 Samir: good point. the snapshot uses the same key material but the in-memory KV references tokens that are bound to a session id. if rotation occurs mid-flight, some cache entry lookups will fail and fall back to rehydrate. that rehydrate is cheap normally but at scale caused queueing.
03:20 Maya: is there a way to snapshot the KV entries to S3 during the test so we can replay in isolation?
03:28 Samir: yes, we can export a sanitized kv snapshot (no PHI) and give you back a compressed file we can re-inject in staging workers. note: injection proto is internal but we'll document it.
03:45 Jamie: we should also capture timeline logs: sidecar traces, worker flamegraphs, autoscaler events, and engine-level metrics. please add those to the checklist.
03:58 Jordan: customer comms — if the dry-run finds a regression we need to have a comms template for impacted customers and a proposal for SLA credit. are we drafting that now or after the dry-run?
04:12 Lina: propose we draft a neutral comms template now and have it approved by Priya afterwards. avoids delay if we need to notify.
04:20 Priya: okay i can take a pass and make sure it's compliant. one ask: can redwood provide a SOC2 attestation excerpt relevant to key handling so i can include in the comms if needed?
04:34 Jamie: yes we'll attach the relevant KMS handling excerpt from our compliance pack and a short note on rotation safety.
04:42 Maya: back to the technicals — autoscaler thresholds. we saw many pods spawn then immediate eviction because the eviction threshold was too tight. can we simulate a sudden token surge during the dry-run?
04:58 Samir: yes we'll use a synthetic load generator that mimics the token distribution and long-context sessions. caveat: synthetic loads can under- or over-estimate KV locality so we'll seed the generator with the 3 production prompts you promised.
05:14 Ethan: we'll provide prompts by EOD tomorrow. also we need to test with two quantization profiles, the lower-ram profile and the high-accuracy profile — do we have both in staging?
05:26 Samir: staging has both model variants. the rollback snapshot will be applied to the high-accuracy runtime so we can see differences.
05:33 Maya: ok, timeline proposal: 07-20 run internal dry-run with only Redwood and BlueLoom SRE (no external customers), 07-21 run smoke routing with a small sample of prod-like traffic, 07-22 retro and decision. does that match everyone's availability?
05:48 Jordan: yes that's fine.
05:51 Lina: i'll block the slots and create invites.
05:55 Samir: one more gotcha — if the KMS rotation window overlaps staging run, we could get false positives. Priya, can you confirm rotation windows for the next 72 hours?
06:09 Priya: yes rotation windows are 02:00–03:00 UTC nightly; i'll pause rotation for 07-20/07-21 staging windows.
06:18 Maya: wonderful, that addresses a major confound.
06:22 Jamie: another mitigation we discussed: increase prefix cache TTL for the long-session cohort, and lower eviction aggressiveness for the model worker tier. Samir, what's the risk of memory pressure if TTL increases?
06:36 Samir: there is an increased risk if the cohort grows unbounded; but we plan to set a cohort limit and LRU watermark. for the dry-run we can sandbox the cohort to 200 active sessions so memory delta is capped.
06:50 Ethan: will the dry-run capture heap and jvm-native memory counters? some of our services are polyglot, might be native allocs.
06:59 Samir: yes, we'll capture both worker heap and the native allocator metrics; i'll add the exact metric names to the checklist.
07:10 Maya: regarding logs, redwood's trace ids in the last event were slightly different format than ours which made joins harder; is there a way to include a canonical trace id in the middleware?
07:25 Jamie: we can add a header mapping for trace-id, we'll add it to the runbook as 'canonical_trace_id' header. Samir will include mapping examples.
07:35 Jordan: competitor question — did we consider the config change Nimbus suggested earlier (aggressive prefetching)? i worry prefetching might make the rehydrate problem worse.
07:47 Samir: yes we discussed it; prefetch helps cold starts but can accelerate contention on the KV store if mis-sized. our bias for now is conservative prefetch and tune after dry-run.
07:59 Maya: anything else on infra?
08:02 Priya: only one more security ask: during export of sanitized KV we need an HMAC digest so we can verify integrity. does redwood support HMAC signing of artifacts?
08:13 Samir: yes we can sign the export with an HMAC; will include verification steps.
08:19 Jamie: excellent. let's run through the explicit checklist now (Samir, read each line and confirm).
08:24 Samir: checklist line 1: pause KMS rotation — confirmed (Priya)
08:28 Maya: confirmed
08:30 Samir: line 2: seed prompts and generator config — confirmed (BlueLoom & Redwood)
08:35 Samir: line 3: export sanitized kv pre-run snapshot — action Samir/Jamie will deliver
08:40 Samir: line 4: apply rollback snapshot in staging and route smoke — Samir to execute, Maya to observe
08:46 Samir: line 5: capture flamegraphs and sidecar traces — Samir to ensure retention 30 days
08:51 Lina: line 6: customer comms template drafted — Lina will circulate
08:55 Jamie: ok wrap — any final Qs?
08:58 Ethan: just one: if rollback shows no improvement are we prepared to escalate to dedicated capacity or is that premature?
09:09 Jamie: we discussed dedicated as a plan B; we'll catalog unit economics and ops overhead, but decision depends on root cause. if evictions persist despite TTL tuning we will explore dedicated pools for the cohort.
09:25 Maya: thanks all. appreciate the careful dry-run.
09:29 Jamie: thanks — i'll follow up with the runbook and invites; see you in the staging window.
09:35 [meeting end]
